PL-44.body: The ring is drawn here by its source page’s own code (the record atlas on the Mindgut launch page). Each dial is one of that page’s own controls: its three finishes, field variation, and which of the record’s ten turns is shown.
PL-44.colorHint: These are the inks the ring’s own drawing calls use: the crossing dots, the address in the center, its caption and the contour. The thermal and engraved fills are laid pixel by pixel and keep their own colors.

ctl.label: Finish
ctl.note: The page’s three renderings: 1 engraving, 2 by number, 3 thermal field.

ctl.label: Field variation
ctl.note: The page’s field-variation slider: stirs the color inside the cut contour; the held coordinates stay put.

ctl.label: Turn
ctl.note: Which of the record’s ten turns of 42 crossings the ring shows.

PL-14.body: The ring is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Lab 2 of the Mindgut Exhibition). Each dial is one of that lab’s own controls: tilt, strands, breath, radial gain, the layer it is drawn in, and the recall chords.

ctl.label: Tilt
ctl.note: The lab’s tilt: 0 looks down the axis, 90 sees the record from the side.

ctl.label: Strands
ctl.note: How many strands of the record are drawn (each line seeds one strand).

ctl.label: Breath
ctl.note: How many of the newest exchanges are in focus: the lab breathes from 4 to 7.

ctl.label: Radial gain
ctl.note: How far each strand reaches from the ring for its weight.

ctl.label: Layer
ctl.note: The lab’s four layers: 1 dots, 2 path, 3 contours, 4 glow.

ctl.label: Recall chords
ctl.note: 1 draws the chords that run from the newest strand back to the ones it recalls; 0 hides them.

PL-126.body: The figure is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Crystal optics territory, plate 01). Each dial is one of the page’s own controls: the defect, the polarizer angle, the retardance and the 530 nm plate.

ctl.label: Defect
ctl.note: 1 Maltese cross (s = +1, four brushes), 2 two half-defects (s = ±½, two brushes each), 3 schlieren field.

ctl.label: Polarizer angle
ctl.note: Turns the crossed polarizers; the brushes turn with them.

ctl.label: Retardance
ctl.note: How far the slow ray falls behind: more retardance, more interference orders.

ctl.label: 530 nm plate
ctl.note: 1 inserts the first-order red plate: blue and yellow quadrants tell the sign of the defect.

PL-148.body: The drawing is made here by its source page’s own code (reference 010, built from the concept end). Each dial is one of the page’s own switches: each pass of the grammar on or off, and the drawing without the grammar.

ctl.label: Fills
ctl.note: 1 lays the flat fills; 0 takes them out.

ctl.label: Stacks
ctl.note: 1 draws the stacked forms; 0 takes them out.

ctl.label: Marks
ctl.note: 1 lays the marks; 0 takes them out.

ctl.label: Key
ctl.note: 1 draws the keyline; 0 takes it out.

ctl.label: Texture
ctl.note: 1 lays the texture pass; 0 leaves the drawing flat.

ctl.label: Without the grammar
ctl.note: 1 draws the same subject without the measured grammar, for comparison.

PL-57.body: The stack is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Mindgut landing page V01). The dial is the page’s own four steps.

ctl.label: Step
ctl.note: The page’s four steps: 1 say, 2 count, 3 keep, 4 reach back.

PL-55.body: The field is drawn here by its source page’s own code (Mindgut Worlds V2), with the type the page sets over it. Each dial is one of the page’s own controls: the world and Mir’s presence state.

ctl.label: World
ctl.note: The page’s three worlds: 1 Frequency (signal as sculpture), 2 Afterimage (memory), 3 Redline (words under pressure).

ctl.sel: main:nth-child(2) > section:nth-child(5) > div:nth-child(1) > div:nth-child(1) > div:nth-child(4) > button
ctl.label: Presence
ctl.note: The page’s three presence states: 1 listening, 2 reaching, 3 at rest.
